title: Production and purification of infectious diseases-associated tetramer for staining of CD8+ T cells from PBMCs
protocol: Unfreeze the bacteria pellet at 20°C–24°C until it starts to melt followed by weighing the cell pellet.
Transfer immediately to ice.
Resuspend and spin the pellet in 10 mL/g of Ordinary Wash Buffer (pH8).
Sonicate by setting the power at 400 watts for 10 min, alternating the tubes and keeping the samples on ice between each sonication cycle.
Centrifuge the solution at 12,000 g for 20 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and repeat resuspending, sonicating, and centrifuging steps twice.
Discard the supernatant and repeat step b to c five times after replacing the Ordinary Wash buffer in step b with a 2 M Urea Wash Buffer (pH8).
Discard the supernatant and repeat step b to c twice after replacing the Ordinary Wash buffer in step b with a 25 mM Tris-HCl.
Add denaturation solution, place a magnetic stir bar into it, and stir overnight at 2°C–8°C.
Centrifuge the solution at 12,000 g for 20 min at 4°C.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.22 μm-pore membrane with a syringe.
Load the sample into the pre-equilibrated Nickel Column at a 1 mL/min rate.
Wash the column with 15×bed column of Nickel Column Clean Buffer as fraction.
Elute the protein of interest with 6×bed volume of Nickel Column Elute Buffer as fraction.
Collect 6 number of aliquots of 10 ml (as shown in Figures).
Take a sample of 60 μL to test for the presence of the protein of interested.
Analyze aliquots of the fractions and the LMW protein ladder by 15% SDS-PAGE.
Stain the gel with Coomassie blue, using the protocol provided by the manufacturer.
Pool fraction 1 and fraction 2.
Determine the absorbance at 280 nm in a nanodrop using an aliquot of the pooled fractions to determine the concentration of the protein of interest.
Use the Nickel Column Elute Buffer as a blank for the absorbance measurement.
Add 0.2% phenylmethanesulfonyl fluoride (PMSF) to inhibit protein degradation.
Store the protein at -80°C for up to 2 months.
Distribute the protein into several tubes to avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles.
Once thawed, store the protein at 4°C and use it within a week.
Analyze the purity of HLA-A2 α chain and β2m by 15% SDS-PAGE.
Generate the HLA-A2 α chain and β2m peptide monomer.
Check the integrity of the refolded protein by Enzyme Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA).
Mix HLA-A2 α chain, β2m, and peptide in a 1:2:10 molar ratio.
Dilute the mixture into 40 mL of refolding solution.
Place a magnetic stir bar into the solution and stir gently at 2°C–8°C for 12 hours.
Dialyze the folding mixture against 25 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0) for 72 hours at 4°C, replacing the dialysate 4–5 times during this period.
Rinse the ultrafiltration tube with filtered water.
Centrifuge the ultrafiltration tube containing 10 mL of filtered water at 3,000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C and discard the lower layer of liquid.
Add 10 mL of sample to the ultrafiltration tube and centrifuge at 3,000 g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Extend the centrifugation time until the upper liquid volume is approximately 1 mL.
Collect the sample and transfer it into a new EP tube.
Temporarily store the sample at 4°C before purification by the Sephacryl S-200 column.
Turn on chromatography instrument 1 hour earlier.
Immerse the inlet tube of the Sephacryl S-200 column in the sample.
Start the pump at a flow rate of 0.5 mL/min.
Quickly turn off the pump when the sample is almost exhausted to avoid air bubbles.
Gently place the inlet tubing into cold filtered and degassed 25 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0).
Restart the pump at a flow rate of 0.5 mL/min.
Change the flow rate to 1 mL/min after 10 minutes.
Collect all peaks appearing in the displayer, particularly the second peak which is the target protein.
Take a sample of 60 μL from each collected peak to test for the presence of the protein of interest.
Prepare fresh biotinylation solution as described in the protocol.
Incubate the reaction mixture at 30°C for 30–40 minutes.
Add BSA (0.5% final concentration) and PMSF (0.2 mM final concentration) for long-term storage.
Aliquot the biotinylated monomer solution into several tubes.
Store aliquoted biotinylated monomer at -80°C for up to 1 year.
Protect the monomer combined with photosensitive peptide from light.
Coat a wells plate with 100 μL streptavidin solution (2 μg/mL).
Seal the plate and incubate overnight (16 h–18 h) at room temperature (18°C–25°C).
Discard the coating solution and wash the plate 3 times with at least 300 μL Wash Buffer per well.
Remove residual buffer by firmly tapping plate upside down on absorbent paper.
Add 300 μL of 1× Dilution Buffer to all wells for blocking non-specific binding.
Seal the plate and incubate it for 30 min at room temperature (18°C–25°C).
Dilute the sample 1,200-fold in 1×Dilution Buffer.
Mix thoroughly.
Discard the Dilution Buffer from the plate.
Blot the residual buffer.
Pipette 100 μL of 1× Dilution buffer or sample into appropriate wells.
Seal the plates and incubate for 1 h at 37°C.
Discard liquid from the wells.
Wash the wells 3 times with 300 μL of wash buffer per well.
Dilute HRP-conjugated antibody to 0.3 μg/mL in 1× Dilution Buffer.
Add 100 μL of diluted HRP-conjugated β2m antibody per well.
Seal the plates and incubate for 1 h at 37°C.
Discard liquid from the wells.
Wash the wells 3 times with 300 μL of wash buffer per well.
Add 100 μL of substrate solution to each well.
Incubate for 8 min at room temperature (18°C–25°C) in the dark while shaking at 450 rpm.
Add 50 μL of stop solution to each well.
Read results at 405 nm on an ELISA reader within 30 min.
Bring tetramers, peptides and PE-conjugated streptavidin to 0°C by putting them on ice.
Dilute 1 mg/mL stock solutions of peptides to 100 μg/mL if monomer is loaded with a photosensitive peptide.
Mix diluted peptides and photosensitive-peptide monomer in a V bottom plate.
Irradiate the mixture with UV light for 40 minutes at a distance of 2-5 cm.
Seal the plate and incubate it for 30 min at 37°C in the dark.
Transfer 30 μL of peptide-exchange monomer into a 0.2 mL tube.
Add 3.3 μL of 0.2 mg/mL PE-conjugated streptavidin and mix by pipetting up-and-down.
Incubate on ice in the dark for 30 min.
Prepare a blocking solution by adding 1.6 μL 50 mM D-Biotin to 198.4 μL PBS and mixing by vortexing.
Add 2.4 μL of blocking solution to stop the reaction.
Incubate the tubes at 2°C–8°C overnight.
Harvest 2–4 × 10^8 T2A2 cells from T-75 cell culture flasks.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 400 g and 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in complete Iscove’s Modified Dulbecco’s Medium (IMDM) to a final concentration of approximately 1–2 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Transfer T2A2 cells in 2 mL/well into a 6-well plate.
Incubate T2A2 cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 30 min after adding mitomycin C (20 μg/mL).
Wash the cells twice with PBS and centrifuge for 5 min at 400 g and 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in 1 mL of PBS containing 5 μM CFSE.
Incubate CFSE-labeled T2A2 cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 30 min.
Wash the cells twice with PBS after incubation.
Discard the supernatant and adjust cell concentration to 5 cells/mL in serum-free IMDM.
Seed T2A2 cells into a 96-well plate with 10^5 cells in 200 μL per well.
Incubate the seeded cells at 37°C for 4 h with peptides at a final concentration of 20 μM.
Use EasySepTM human CD8 positive selection kit to pre-sort CD8+ T cells from PBMCs of HLA-A2+ healthy donors.
Mix harvested peptide-loaded T2A2 cells with sorted CD8+ T cells.
Centrifuge the mixture at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in primary T medium to a final concentration of approximately 2.5 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Add 2.5 × 10^5 peptide-loaded T2A2 cells with 2.5 × 10^5 CD8+ T cells plus anti-human CD28 (1 μg/mL) and IL-2 (50 IU/mL) in 96-well plates for co-culture.
Supplement the culture medium with 50 IU/mL IL-2 and 20 μM peptide every two days.
Perform tetramer staining analysis 7 days later.
Collect cells from 96-well plates and wash them with PBS containing 1% BSA.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 600 g and 4°C.
Stain with 10 μL antigen-specific tetramer for 1 h at room temperature.
Add 2 μL APC-labeled human CD8+ (clone T8) for 1 h on ice.
Wash once.
Perform flow cytometric analysis.
